newsitem.title: UK: Labour hits 50 percent support in Scots poll.
newsitem.headline: Labour hits 50 percent support in Scots poll.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party jumped three points in a week to hit 50 percent support from Scottish voters, according to the latest opinion poll for The Herald newspaper on Wednesday.
The System Three poll showed the ruling Conservatives down one to 14 percent while the Scottish National Party (SNP) gained two to 26 percent.
The Liberal Democrats dropped three points to nine percent.
The poll was carried out in 40 of Scotland's 72 parliamentary constituencies on April 26-27. Of those interviewed 19 percent refused to say how they would vote on May 1 or were undecided.
Labour won 49 Scottish seats in 1992. The Conservatives took 11, the Liberal Democrats nine and SNP three.
